structured.what_it_does: Likha-Klima is the CCC’s tentative title for a one-day culmination Innovation Showcase of the Youth Climate Leadership Accelerator Project—not a single student product. University-based youth complete five accelerator modules (in-person Saturdays plus asynchronous work in November 2025), a Masterclass (planned 22 Nov 2025 during Climate Change Consciousness Week), and a “Meeting of the Brains” prep session, then exhibit climate adaptation/mitigation and advocacy innovations in an exhibit-plus-pavilion format for invited youth, academe, NGOs, and government. A Young Climate Innovators’ (and Campaigners’) Circle community of practice is planned to launch at or after the showcase, with a recognition ceremony closing the accelerator.
structured.place: Philippines (Metro Manila–focused pilot; CCC office listed at First Residences Bldg., JP Laurel St., Malacañang Comp., San Miguel, Manila; sessions with host/partner universities)
structured.outcome_or_award: Planned recognition ceremony and launch of Young Climate Innovators/Campaigners Circle; no public placement winners or award results verified under the Likha-Klima name
structured.gap: No public confirmation that the showcase was actually held under the final name “Likha-Klima” (title was explicit as tentative in the TOR). No verified list of final participating universities/teams, individual student builders, Masterclass speakers, consulting firm awarded under ITB 2025-005, PhilGEPS award notice, post-event press coverage, terminal report, or specific project innovations/placements. Possible university list (UST, Miriam College, DLSU, Mapúa, Ateneo de Manila, PUP, PLM, Taguig City University, UP) is aspirational/possible in the TOR only—not confirmed enrollment. Secondary Facebook mentions of YCLAP partnerships (e.g., PLV, Taguig) not fully verifiable from primary CCC pages in this pass.
structured.note: For Youth CLAP desk: treat Likha-Klima as CCC program infrastructure (showcase + accelerator), not a competing student climate-tech product. Parent program aligns closely with Ateneo Youth CLAP naming (YCLAP). TOR target: up to 10 universities, max 3 orgs/school, 4 students/org; modules on climate policy/agreements, youth movements, leadership, advocacy tools. Design Reference Group may include NYC, CHED, Climate Reality Philippines, AIM, UNICEF, NPTE/academe, private-sector climate expert. ABC for consulting services: Php 1,700,000. Do not invent winners or school teams; follow up on CCC BAC (bac@climate.gov.ph) / PhilGEPS for award and any post-Dec 2025 terminal report.
